review_method: Review changed replies and citations against the question and book text. The three target cases were already known and guided the changes. Preserve earlier correctness judgments when a reply and citation match. Review every reply on the separate check.

changed_replies.prompt: What else did he say fell along with them?

changed_replies.prompt: How do they mend when the roofs crack?
changed_replies.expected: They grow together again over time.

before.reply: I couldn't find an answer supported by the book.
before.reader_query: How do they mend when the roofs crack (context: long did it take the glass houses in the Mangaboo city to grow so large)?

after.reply: No; but they will grow together again, in time, and we must wait until they do.
after.reader_query: How do they mend when the roofs crack (context: long did it take the glass houses in the Mangaboo city to grow so large)?

reread.query: What will they do if the people cannot mend them?
reread.excerpt: "Of course," he replied. "But it took a good many years for them to grow as large and fine as they are now. That is why we are so angry when a Rain of Stones comes to break our towers and crack our roofs." "Can't you mend them?" she enquired. "No; but they will grow together again, in time, and we must wait until they do."

changed_replies.review: The adjacent question and answer distinguish how the roofs mend from how long the houses took to grow. The reply now includes both the method and the wait.

changed_replies.expected: He thought the place was dangerous and unfit for living creatures. Everything looked dead.

reread.query: Why did Jim want them to go down again?
reread.excerpt: "Everything," grumbled the horse. "I've taken a look at this place, and it's no fit country for real creatures to go to. Everything's dead, up there--no flesh or blood or growing thing anywhere." "Never mind; we can't turn back," said Dorothy; "and we don't intend to stay there, anyhow." "It's dangerous," growled Jim, in a stubborn tone.

after.reply: It's dangerous. I've taken a look at this place, and it's no fit country for real creatures to go to. Everything's dead, up there--no flesh or blood or growing thing anywhere.

reread.query: Why did Jim think it was dangerous?
reread.excerpt: "Everything," grumbled the horse. "I've taken a look at this place, and it's no fit country for real creatures to go to. Everything's dead, up there--no flesh or blood or growing thing anywhere."

changed_replies.review: The same passage attributes the danger to Jim and records his explanation that the country was dead and unfit for living creatures.
